hints.title: Find where either factor is zero
hints.body: Solve 1+2cosx=0 and cos(2x)=0 within the stated interval.
hints.recap: Factor zeros split a product into intervals for sign checks.
hints.pitfall: For the second equation, solve for 2x first, then divide the angles by 2.
hints.pause: Put all the zero points in order on one number line.

recall.reminder: Factor zeros split a product into intervals for sign checks.

hints.title: Give each factor its own sign row
hints.body: On each interval, mark the sign of each factor. Multiply the two signs to find the sign of y.
hints.recap: A negative product has one positive and one negative factor.
hints.pitfall: A factor zero gives y=0, so it is excluded from a strictly negative result.
hints.pause: Keep the intervals with negative products and check all their endpoints.

recall.reminder: A negative product has one positive and one negative factor.

solution:
Within 0<x<π, 1+2cosx=0 at x=2π3. It is positive before that point and negative afterwards. The factor cos2x vanishes at π4 and 3π4; it is negative between them and positive elsewhere in the given domain.

The product is therefore negative on (π4, 2π3), where the first factor is positive and the second negative, and on (3π4, π), where the signs are reversed. Between 2π3 and 3π4 both are negative, so that interval is excluded.

The full answer is π4<x<2π3 or 3π4<x<π, option D.
